extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians and open-mic performers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice for new and developing stand-up comedians on why they 'bomb' on stage and what to change to improve laughs and presence at open mics and club shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge about how to develop and deliver a quality stand-up comedy act
rubrics_metrics.description: Because most new comedians have only seen or experienced 'polished and refined' stand-up comedy that 'appears' as if the comedian is simply talking 'off the top of their head'… They are under the false impression that stand-up comedy is far easier than it appears, not realizing that it takes considerable knowledge and skill to develop and deliver a stand-up comedy act that gets noteworthy laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume polished stage work is effortless; learn the craft and techniques required to develop and deliver material that elicits laughs. (Page suggests formal lessons/courses such as the 'Killer Stand-up Online Course' for actionable learning.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of preparation before performing
rubrics_metrics.description: One need only attend any stand-up comedy open mic night anywhere in the world to see firsthand just how ill prepared new comedians are when it comes to delivering a stand-up comedy act that even has a chance of getting decent laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare material and stage delivery before performing; avoid showing up under-rehearsed, especially at open mics where many performers demonstrate this anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trying to 'write' their way to being funny on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians who only focus on the words and sentences they are going to use on stage automatically limit themselves to 7% of their laughter power potential on stage – which sets them up for long term bombing as a comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't focus solely on written lines; work on delivery, timing, physicality and other non-verbal elements that create laughs. Treat writing as one part of performance craft, not the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivering the same unfunny material expecting it to get funnier with 'age'
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering the same unfunny material expecting it to get funnier with 'age'. Once again, you need only visit a couple of comedy open mic nights featuring the same comedians to see this bombing activity in action — bombing activity that has gone on for years in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterate and replace material that doesn't work rather than repeating it indefinitely; test, revise, and retire jokes that chronically fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not enough comedy talent to be a comedian
rubrics_metrics.description: While most people who attempt stand-up comedy have all the comedy talent they need, there are always a number of folks who want to be a comedian but don’t have the comedy talent God gave an ingrown toenail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic about natural aptitude; recognize that talent limits exist and you cannot 'write' your way to more innate comedic talent. Consider alternate roles or focus on strengths where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombing is often self-inflicted and obscured by lack of feedback ('silent public humiliation')
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombing on stage as a comedian is mostly a self-inflicted experience... there seems to be some sort of unwritten rule that one does not comment on an individual’s failed sense of humor or a less than optimal stand-up comedy performance, which basically leaves a comedian in the dark about how awful their stand-up comedy performance actually was on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek explicit, actionable feedback because audiences and peers often won't tell you when you bomb; be proactive in getting critique from knowledgeable sources (club owners, agents, coaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombing is usually easily overcome with the right actionable information and full use of one's comedy talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Ironically, bombing onstage as a comedian is primarily a self-inflicted affair (for the majority of those who do have plenty of comedy talent) that is usually easily overcome with the right actionable information when it comes to developing and delivering a professional stand-up comedy routine that capitalizes on ALL of an individual’s comedy talent right from the start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue structured, actionable training and resources to develop and deliver professional routines; capitalize on all aspects of your comedic ability (writing, delivery, timing, stage presence) to reduce bombing risk. (The page recommends the author's free lessons/course as an example resource.)
